purpose: W8-C: add a server-authoritative settings registry with scope inheritance, effective-value provenance and durable developer/API-key/webhook settings while refusing to expose configuration for underlying authorities that are not yet implemented.
authorization: Owner instruction on 2026-09-05 to continue PC-CROP. Staged only; no implementation authority before separate governance review/merge and immutable base-state promotion.

excludedAfterSourceAudit.reason: Identity, registration, membership and Role Eligibility are source authorities only and remain unchanged.
Provider/integration settings reference accepted registry/binding authority; W8-C does not mutate provider maturity or credentials.
Finance settings cannot create or alter obligations/SettlementPlan; only settings explicitly declared by accepted finance policy may be surfaced later.
Signature settings cannot invent signing authority/provider activation; only accepted provider/mode choices may be configured after W5-B.
Initial settings module mounting may be separately bounded; staged authority focuses on registry and UI subtree.
Unsupported privacy claims are removed only in a separate governance/privacy slice; settings must not perpetuate them as facts.

requiredInvariants: Settings are data/configuration authority only within their declared scope and never replace domain command authority. A setting may configure policy/choice only when the underlying domain declares that setting as supported.

Scopes are explicit and versioned: PLATFORM_DEFAULT, TENANT, ORGANIZATION, ROLE/JOB_PROFILE where allowed and USER. Every key declares which scopes may override it and the deterministic precedence order.

Every effective value returns provenance: definition version, winning scope/object, value revision, overridden ancestors, actor/reason and effective timestamp. The UI cannot show an unexplained merged value.
Settings definitions are typed, versioned, validated, secret/non-secret classified and include visibility/write authority. Unknown keys or caller-defined schemas are rejected.

Secret values are never returned in plaintext after initial generation and are stored only through approved secret/key handling. Settings rows store references/fingerprints, not provider credentials in browser-visible JSON.

API keys and outbound webhook subscriptions move from process-local Maps into durable tenant/organization-scoped authority with hashed secrets, expiry/revocation, scoped permissions, allowed-destination policy, immutable issuance/revocation receipts and no plaintext secret listing.

Creating an API key/webhook requires current membership/capability and recent MFA when policy declares it high-risk. Revoked membership cannot replay an old issuance/revocation receipt as current authority.

Personal notification/locale/display preferences can be user-scoped; organization commercial/integration/security settings require organization authority; platform owner settings require staff/control-plane authority. Scope escalation is impossible through payload fields.

Finance, signature, government, EDO, ATI, 1C and provider settings show NOT_AVAILABLE/NOT_ACTIVATED until the corresponding accepted domain capability/integration binding exists. A toggle cannot activate an external adapter.

Settings history is append-only/versioned. Changing a setting creates a new revision; effective-value history remains reproducible for audit and cannot rewrite the configuration that governed a past Deal/document/payment.
Preference inheritance never applies to legally significant immutable source snapshots retroactively; domain commands pin the effective settings/policy revision they actually consumed.
Developer API/webhook outbound URLs use the existing server-side allowlist/SSRF policy and durable delivery/replay authority; browser validation is presentation-only.
No hard-coded local-only privacy/processor claim becomes server truth merely by being placed under settings.
Registration, Role Eligibility, Federal Accounting lock #4321, external provider credentials and REG.RU production topology remain unchanged.
acceptance: Domain/PostgreSQL tests prove definition typing, allowed scopes, deterministic inheritance and exact effective-value provenance across platform/tenant/org/user examples.
Unauthorized scope escalation, cross-tenant access, stale revision, changed-payload replay and revoked actor authority fail closed.
Historical effective-value snapshots remain reproducible after parent/child settings change.
API key tests prove durable issuance, one-time plaintext return, hash verification, expiry, revocation, scope validation and no plaintext listing after creation.
Webhook subscription tests prove durable storage, destination allowlist, hashed/one-time secret, revocation and tenant isolation; restart/second-instance behavior matches one authority.
UI tests show source/provenance and inherited/overridden state for every editable setting and never present unavailable external integrations as active toggles.
No registration/Role Eligibility/accounting lock files are changed and settings cannot directly execute a money/signature/regulatory/provider command.
Exact-head CI/review plus REG.RU settings/API-key/webhook runtime evidence are required before terminal SETTINGS credit.
remainingTerminalBoundary: Full per-domain setting definitions depend on each accepted underlying authority and are added only with that domain's consumer integration.
Privacy/data-subject governance, notification center, role workspace and Gekta settings have separate terminal requirements.
Real external credentials remain managed through approved secret/integration binding flows, not this registry.
Human usability/accessibility acceptance across the complete settings tree remains later UX work.
